verdict.rationale: Secureframe's MCP docs show that an agent client gets its own token after a user signs in and approves access, and an API key option exists for headless setups such as CI jobs and scripts. Nothing in the evidence shows these credentials can be limited by permission scope, role, read-only access, or resource. Missing for 10: documented permission scopes or least-privilege controls on tokens or API keys, read-only versus write restrictions, credential revocation and rotation, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: you sign in to Secureframe and approve access, and the client receives its own token. There is nothing to generate, copy, or store yourself, and no secret ends up in a config file.
API key For setups with no browser — CI jobs, scripts, serv
Any MCP-capable client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) can connect, letting you ask an assistant to look things up and take actions on your behalf.
